title: One Thing Visible
pin_title: ADHD Focus: Keep Only One Task in Sight
description: Too many open tabs and lists create noise that freezes action. Close everything except the single next step and let the rest wait out of sight. When the brain sees only one thing, starting feels lighter and the first move stops being a decision. Pair it with permission to stop when the timer ends. Clarity reduces friction more than motivation does. #ADHD #Focus #ADHDTips #OneThing

title: Leave a Note
pin_title: ADHD Memory: Use External Reminders Instead of Hoping
description: Relying on memory alone is hard with ADHD, and hoping to remember is not a plan. Write the next step on a sticky note and put it where you will see it: on the door, the kettle, the bag you carry. The note becomes the reminder, so your brain does not have to hold the plan. Seeing the step makes starting easier than trying to recall it later. #ADHD #Reminders #ADHDTips #ExecutiveFunction

title: See the Win
pin_title: ADHD Motivation: Make Progress Visible With One Small Mark
description: ADHD brains need a clear signal that something happened. After a small step, mark it in a way you can see: a check, a star, a moved object. Visible progress quiets the feeling that nothing is moving and makes the next start feel more possible, because the evidence is right there in front of you. One mark is enough, and it does not have to be neat. #ADHD #Progress #ADHDTips #Focus

title: Open the Notebook
pin_title: ADHD Start: Open the Notebook and Nothing More
description: The hardest part is often just opening the thing. Make your first action only opening the notebook or the document, then stop if you want. Once it is open, the next sentence is usually easier, and the page no longer feels like a wall. Starting with the tiniest visible action lowers the barrier without asking for motivation first. Open it, look at it, and that counts as a start. #ADHD #Starting #ADHDTips #Focus
